correctness.rationale: In a proper rook coloring, each row and column contains every used color at most once. At a cell, every color other than the cell color therefore appears zero, one, or two times in the open neighborhood according as it lies in neither, exactly one, or both of the row and column color sets; the cell color appears zero times. Thus the odd condition is exactly inequality of those two sets. The unbalanced cyclic construction gives the clique lower bound exactly. In the balanced case, n colors make all row and column sets equal, and with n+1 colors the row-missing and column-missing counts agree for each color, forcing an equal missing color on some row-column pair. The explicit n+2 construction separates distance-two row-missing pairs from consecutive column-missing pairs. Direct computation agrees in all checked cases.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly resolves a canonical missing Cartesian-product family in a recently active coloring invariant. It exhibits a sharp structural phase change: every rectangular rook graph with unequal sides attains the clique lower bound, while the balanced family incurs an unavoidable two-color parity surcharge. The row-column set criterion is a reusable structural lemma linking odd vertex colorings of rook graphs to proper edge-coloring incidence data, and the proof gives explicit optimal constructions.
